target_customer: Developers, designers and engineering teams on macOS (later Windows and iOS)
problem: Non coding tasks in tools like Jira, GitHub and Slack consume a large share of a developer's day and Spotlight is limited.
business_model: Freemium subscription (Pro and Teams) with extension store

founders.name: Thomas Paul Mann
founders.background_notes: Software engineer at those organizations per the YC page.

founders.name: Petr Nikolaev
founders.background_notes: Labelled CTO in the TechCrunch 2024 photo caption; no bio on YC page.

competitors.name: Apple Spotlight
competitors.what: Built in macOS launcher and search

competitors.name: Alfred
competitors.what: Third party macOS launcher with workflows

technical_complexity.rationale: Native macOS app needing fast keyboard first UI and later an extension API; an extensions store shipped in 2021.

defensibility.rationale: Community built more than 100 extensions by Nov 2021 (Series A post), creating a store ecosystem, though launchers were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple did not replicate it through 2025; Raycast reached Windows beta in Nov 2025.

market_need_then: Developers lose time on non coding tasks; the YC page claims up to 50 percent of a developer's day.

identity.logo: Red mark on dark UI; brand red #FF6363
identity.visual_style: Sleek dark chrome with a diagonal red stripe pattern (third party descriptions)

branding.community_and_virality: Public press kit and brand guideline templates; extension community; Product Hunt launch with 390 upvotes in Oct 2020.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong developer mindshare, official press kit and brand guidelines, and a Product Hunt launch; no sourced evidence of mascot or merch.

outcome_analysis: Raycast launched publicly in October 2020 as a faster, extensible alternative to Spotlight and Alfred, then added an extensions API and store that built a community. It raised a 2.7 million seed from Accel, a 15 million Series A in November 2021 and a 30 million Series B in September 2024 to expand to Windows and iOS. It remained independent and the Windows beta opened in November 2025.
notes: Series B lead conflicts across sources (one says Atomico) so investors left empty. A third party blog valuation above 100M is unverified. The seed amount and date come from search summaries of TechCrunch, with the Series A post stating Accel invested at seed. The Alfred and Spotlight entries rely on Raycast launch materials positioning (secondary summaries), not a dated Alfred source. Competitor sources are dated 2020-10, about three months after the as_of date, because the public launch was then.
